items.title: Two-group logrank and weighted logrank scores
items.statement: For two groups, define the risk-set event counts, pooled risk-set expectation, conditional hypergeometric variance, weighted score, variance estimate, normal-calibrated statistic, and the distinct exact randomization ordering. State tie and null-model conventions.

items.title: Uniform convergence of empirical risk-set fractions
items.statement: For iid observed times in each of two groups, the empirical fractions at risk converge uniformly on a fixed finite horizon to their population risk probabilities. Verify pointwise measurability, the unit envelope, and finite L1 bracketing entropy for the threshold class.

items.title: Conditional hypergeometric moments for a logrank risk set
items.statement:
Fix a risk set with $Y_1$ group-1 subjects, $Y_0$ group-0 subjects, and
$Y=Y_1+Y_0$. Conditional on the margins, suppose the $d$ failing subjects
are a uniform $d$-subset of these $Y$ subjects, where $0\le d\le Y$. Let
$O$ be the number of failures in group 1. If $Y>1$, then
$$ \mathbb E[O]=d\frac{Y_1}{Y},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(O)=\frac{Y_1Y_0d(Y-d)}{Y^2(Y-1)}. $$
If $Y=0$ or $Y=1$, set the contribution to the variance to zero; the
expectation remains $dY_1/Y$ when $Y>0$, and is zero when $Y=0$.

For the sequential assertion, take a finite sequence $j=1,\ldots,J$ on a
probability space with a filtration
$\mathcal H_0\subseteq\mathcal H_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal H_J$.
Before the failures at step $j$ are revealed, the current risk-set subjects,
their group counts $Y_{1j},Y_{0j}$, and the total $d_j$ are
$\mathcal H_{j-1}$-measurable, with $0\le d_j\le Y_j:=Y_{1j}+Y_{0j}$.
Conditionally on $\mathcal H_{j-1}$, the failing subjects are a uniform
$d_j$-subset of the current $Y_j$ subjects; their identities are revealed
in $\mathcal H_j$. If $Y_j=0$, necessarily $d_j=0$ and the failing subset is
empty. Put $E_j=d_jY_{1j}/Y_j$ when $Y_j>0$ and $E_j=0$ when $Y_j=0$;
let $V_j$ be the displayed risk-set variance when $Y_j>1$ and zero when
$Y_j\le1$. Suppose each real weight $w_j$ is $\mathcal H_{j-1}$-measurable
and
$$\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{j=1}^Jw_j^2V_j\right]<\infty.$$
Then $D_j=w_j(O_j-E_j)$ are square-integrable martingale differences and
$$ \mathbb E\!\left[\sum_jD_j\right]=0,\qquad \operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_jD_j\right) =\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_jw_j^2V_j\right], $$
where the nonempty-risk-set variance contribution is the one in
[[def-logrank-risk-set-score-and-test]].

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 6: Logrank Test, PDF pp. 3-4
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.3, PDF pp. 59-60

items.title: Uniform convergence of the risk-set treatment fraction
items.statement:
For each $g\in\{0,1\}$, let $(U_{gi})_{i\ge1}$ be IID measurable
$[0,\infty)$-valued observed times with law $P_g$; independence between
the two groups is not required. Along a sequence of deterministic positive
sample sizes, let $n=n_0+n_1\to\infty$ and
$n_g/n\to\rho_g\in(0,1)$, where $\rho_0+\rho_1=1$. Set
$s_g(t):=P_g(U_{g1}\ge t)$, $y_g(t)=\rho_gs_g(t)$, and
$y(t)=y_0(t)+y_1(t)$. Assume $\inf_{0\le t\le\tau}y(t)>0$. Write
$$ Y_{g,n}(t)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}1\{U_{gi}\ge t\},\qquad p_n(t)=\begin{cases} Y_{1,n}(t)/(Y_{0,n}(t)+Y_{1,n}(t)),&Y_{0,n}(t)+Y_{1,n}(t)>0,\\ 0,&Y_{0,n}(t)+Y_{1,n}(t)=0. \end{cases} $$
Then, for $g=0,1$,
$$ \sup_{t\le\tau}\left|\frac{Y_{g,n}(t)}n-y_g(t)\right|\longrightarrow_P0, $$
and
$$ \sup_{0\le t\le\tau}\left|p_n(t)-\bar z(t)\right|\longrightarrow_P0, \qquad \bar z(t):=\frac{y_1(t)}{y(t)}. $$

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 13: Large Sample Theory for 2-Sample Tests, PDF pp. 1-6
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.4, PDF pp. 61-62

items.title: The logrank ordering gives a valid Fisher randomization p-value
items.statement:
Fix a finite randomized treatment-assignment model with allowed assignments
$\mathcal Z$ and known law $p$, with unit set $\mathcal I$ as in
[[def-finite-randomized-treatment-assignment-model]]. Fix a map
$\gamma:\mathcal Z\to\{0,1\}^{\mathcal I}$ assigning each allowed assignment
a binary logrank group map. For each subject $i$, let
$(U_i(z),\delta_i(z))\in[0,\tau]\times\{0,1\}$ be the full right-censored
record under assignment $z$. Assume the **record sharp null**: for every $i$,
the pair $(U_i(z),\delta_i(z))$ is constant over all $z\in\mathcal Z$. Fix
before observing assignment or records a bounded logrank weight rule and the
two-sided ordering $T(z)=|U_w(\gamma(z);U,\delta)|$.

The inclusive assignment-tail p-value
$$ p_{\rm rand}(z):=\sum_{z'\in\mathcal Z}p(z') 1\{|U_w(\gamma(z');U,\delta)|\ge |U_w(\gamma(z);U,\delta)|\} $$
is superuniform under the assignment law, so it is a valid finite-sample
p-value for the record sharp null. If an auxiliary $V$ is independent of
the assignment and uniform on $[0,1]$, replacing the inclusive tail by the
strict-tail mass plus $V$ times the tied-score mass gives an exactly uniform
p-value. The result uses the actual assignment probabilities and asserts no
validity under a weak average-effect null or under an equal-hazard null alone.

references.title: Siva Balakrishnan, CMU 36-705 Lecture 28: Fisher's Exact p-values, §28.5, PDF pp. 4-6

items.title: Weighted logrank score expansion under a common-hazard model
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n_0,n_1$ be deterministic, $n=n_0+n_1$,
and let $Z_i=g$ for subject $i$ in group $g\in\{0,1\}$. On a common
finite-horizon filtration, each subject has the one-event process
$$N_{gi}(t)=1\{U_{gi}\le t,\ \delta_{gi}=1\},\qquad Y_{gi}(t)=1\{U_{gi}\ge t\},$$
and satisfies the separate counting-process contract
$$A_{gi}(t)=\int_0^tY_{gi}(s)\lambda(s)\,ds,\qquad M_{gi}=N_{gi}-A_{gi},$$
where $\lambda$ is a common deterministic nonnegative hazard density with
$\Lambda(\tau):=\int_0^\tau\lambda(s)\,ds<\infty$. Assume each $M_{gi}$ is
a square-integrable martingale under this contract, $Y_{gi}$ is predictable,
and no two subjects have simultaneous event jumps. Write $N_{g,n}$ and
$Y_{g,n}$ for the group sums, $N_n=N_{0,n}+N_{1,n}$, and
$p_n(t)=Y_{1,n}(t)/(Y_{0,n}(t)+Y_{1,n}(t))$, with $p_n(t)=0$ on an empty
pooled risk set.

Assume the observed-time and allocation hypotheses of
[[lem-logrank-risk-fraction-converges]]: within each group the observed
times are IID, $n\to\infty$, $n_g/n\to\rho_g\in(0,1)$, and, with
$y_g(t)=\rho_gP(U_{g1}\ge t)$ and $y=y_0+y_1$,
$\inf_{0\le t\le\tau}y(t)>0$. Set $\bar z(t)=y_1(t)/y(t)$. Let $w_n$ be a common predictable
weight process with $|w_n(t)|\le C$ and a measurable supremum satisfying
$\sup_{t\le\tau}|w_n(t)-w(t)|\to_P0$ for a deterministic bounded predictable
weight $w$. Then the weighted logrank score satisfies
$$\frac{U_{n,w_n}}{\sqrt n} =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{g=0}^1\sum_{i=1}^{n_g} \int_0^\tau w(t)\bigl(g-\bar z(t)\bigr)\,dM_{gi}(t)+o_P(1).$$
In particular, fixed deterministic bounded predictable weights are included
by taking $w_n=w$.

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 13: Large Sample Theory for 2-Sample Tests, PDF pp. 2-7
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.3, PDF pp. 59-60

items.title: Consistency of the weighted logrank variance estimate
items.statement:
Assume the two-group common-hazard model with finite-horizon predictable
risk processes and the explicit square-integrable martingale contracts
$M_{gi}=N_{gi}-A_{gi}$, $A_{gi}(t)=\int_0^tY_{gi}(s)\lambda(s)\,ds$; assume
no simultaneous event jumps. Let $Y_{g,n}=\sum_iY_{gi}$,
$Y_n=Y_{0,n}+Y_{1,n}$, and assume the uniform risk-fraction convergence
$Y_n/n\to y$ and $p_n=Y_{1,n}/Y_n\to\bar z$ in probability on $[0,\tau]$,
with $p_n=0$ on an empty risk set (as proved in
[[lem-logrank-risk-fraction-converges]]). Let $w_n\to w$ uniformly in
probability, where the predictable weights are uniformly bounded and $w$
is deterministic. Suppose event times are continuous, so every observed
failure time has $d_j=1$ almost surely. Here $\widehat V_{n,w_n}$ is the
plug-in statistic defined in [[def-logrank-risk-set-score-and-test]]; the
claim is its asymptotic consistency and does not assert an exact finite-sample
conditional variance law. Here $y_0,y_1$ are deterministic nonnegative Borel functions,
$y=y_0+y_1$, $\inf_{0\le t\le\tau}y(t)>0$, and $\bar z=y_1/y$. Define
$$\sigma_w^2:=\int_0^\tau w(t)^2\frac{y_0(t)y_1(t)}{y(t)}\lambda(t)\,dt.$$
Then the weighted plug-in variance sum from
[[def-logrank-risk-set-score-and-test]] satisfies
$$\frac{\widehat V_{n,w_n}}n\longrightarrow_P\sigma_w^2.$$

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 13: Large Sample Theory for 2-Sample Tests, PDF pp. 4-7
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.3-5.4, PDF pp. 59-62

items.title: Terminal normal limit for weighted logrank scores
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For $g\in\{0,1\}$, let
$(T_{gi},C_{gi})_{i\ge1}$ be IID within group, with
$T_{gi},C_{gi}\in[0,\infty)$ almost surely and the two group families
independent. Assume conditional independent censoring
$T_{gi}\perp C_{gi}\mid g$, and a common absolutely continuous event-time
law with hazard density $\lambda$ on $[0,\tau]$, where
$\Lambda(\tau)=\int_0^\tau\lambda(t)\,dt<\infty$. Censoring distributions
may differ between groups. Use the horizon-truncated record
$U_{gi}:=\min(T_{gi},C_{gi},\tau)$ and
$\delta_{gi}:=1\{T_{gi}\le C_{gi},\ T_{gi}\le\tau\}$, which lies in
$[0,\tau]\times\{0,1\}$ as required by
[[def-logrank-risk-set-score-and-test]].

For deterministic positive sample sizes $n_g$ along a sequence with
$n=n_0+n_1\to\infty$ and $n_1/n\to\rho\in(0,1)$, set
$\rho_1=\rho$, $\rho_0=1-\rho$,
$y_g(t)=\rho_gP(U_{g1}\ge t)$, $y(t)=y_0(t)+y_1(t)$, and
$\bar z(t)=y_1(t)/y(t)$. Assume $\inf_{t\le\tau}y(t)>0$. For each
subject define $N_{gi}(t)=1\{U_{gi}\le t,\delta_{gi}=1\}$ and
$Y_{gi}(t)=1\{U_{gi}\ge t\}$. Under one common filtration, assume $Y_{gi}$
is predictable and, separately, that
$$ A_{gi}(t)=\int_0^tY_{gi}(s)\lambda(s)\,ds,\qquad M_{gi}=N_{gi}-A_{gi} $$
satisfies the finite-horizon square-integrable martingale contract of
[[def-counting-process-intensity-and-compensator-contract]]. Assume no two
subjects have simultaneous event jumps. Conditional independent censoring
and the displayed hazard are scientific model premises; they are not used
as substitutes for the explicit martingale contract.

Use $U_{n,w_n}$ and $\widehat V_{n,w_n}$ as defined in
[[def-logrank-risk-set-score-and-test]]. Let $w_n$ be a common predictable
weight sequence with $|w_n|\le C$ and a measurable supremum satisfying
$\sup_{t\le\tau}|w_n(t)-w(t)|\to_P0$ for a deterministic bounded Borel
predictable weight $w$. Define
$$ \sigma_w^2:=\int_0^\tau w(t)^2\frac{y_0(t)y_1(t)}{y_0(t)+y_1(t)}\lambda(t)\,dt. $$
Then
$$ \frac{U_{n,w_n}}{\sqrt n}\Rightarrow N(0,\sigma_w^2). $$
If $\sigma_w^2>0$, define the standardized statistic as
$U_{n,w_n}/\sqrt{\widehat V_{n,w_n}}$ when the denominator is positive and
assign any fixed finite value on the event that it is zero. Every such
extension converges to $N(0,1)$. If $\sigma_w^2=0$, only the degenerate
score limit is asserted. For a fixed deterministic weight, take $w_n=w$.
This is a terminal finite-dimensional limit; it asserts no process central
limit theorem.

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 13: Large Sample Theory for 2-Sample Tests, PDF pp. 1-12
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.4, PDF pp. 61-62

items.title: Crossing hazards with a zero observed logrank score
items.statement:
Use follow-up horizon $\tau=2.5$. Let the event times be mutually
independent, with group hazards
$$ \lambda_1(t)=\begin{cases}2,&0\le t\le1,\\1,&t>1,\end{cases} \qquad \lambda_0(t)=\begin{cases}1,&0\le t\le1,\\2,&t>1.\end{cases} $$
Let all censoring times be mutually independent and independent of the
entire event-time family. In group 1, let each censoring time equal $1.5$
with probability $2/3$ and $2.5$ with probability $1/3$; in group 0 let it
equal $2.5$. Observe each subject through
$U_i=\min(T_i,C_i)$ and $\delta_i=1\{T_i\le C_i\}$, using the event-censor
tie convention in [[def-logrank-risk-set-score-and-test]]. Since every
$C_i\le\tau$, these records lie in $[0,\tau]\times\{0,1\}$. A possible
sample has
$n_1=4$: one event at $t_1\in(0,1)$, two subjects censored at $1.5$, and
one subject censored at $2.5$. It has $n_0=2$: one event at
$t_2\in(2,2.5)$ and one subject censored at $2.5$. Compute the unweighted
logrank score, its plug-in variance, and the empirical product-limit
curves. Verify that this sample pattern has positive probability and that
the population survival curves cross even though the observed score is zero.
items.strategy: Compute both survival functions and all nonzero risk-set contributions. Verify that the event/censoring ordering has positive probability and that the score cancellation does not establish equality of the survival laws.

items.title: An exact logrank randomization p-value with unequal assignment weights
items.statement:
Fix a follow-up horizon $\tau=3$ and three subjects. For every allowed
assignment $z\in\{e_1,e_2,e_3\}$, where
$\gamma(e_k)_i=1\{i=k\}$ is the binary group map that treats subject $k$,
prescribe the full records
$(U_i(z),\delta_i(z))=(i,1)$ for $i=1,2,3$. Thus the subjects have
uncensored event times $1,2,3$ under every assignment, satisfying the
full-record sharp null. Exactly one subject is treated. The allowed assignments $e_1,e_2,e_3$ treat subject
1, 2, or 3, respectively, with probabilities $1/2,1/3,1/6$. Predeclare unit
weight and the two-sided absolute unweighted logrank score before observing
the assignment. Enumerate all
scores and inclusive assignment-tail p-values and verify superuniformity
under this unequal assignment law.
items.strategy: Recompute the risk sets, score, tail mass, and p-value at all three assignments, then check the exact finite weighted distribution at every threshold.
